title: A Valid Losing Trade
hook: The stop got hit. The trade didn’t change.

launchpad.outcome: Work a trade that is valid on every check, watch it lose, and decide what (if anything) should change.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Does one loss rewrite a valid trade?

slides.kicker: Lesson 3 · A loss isn’t a verdict
slides.headline: Same checks. Different day.
slides.line: Room, PIL, a closed I → C → C, the retest entry, a stop beyond the correction. Every check passes.

slides.kicker: Lesson 3 · A loss isn’t a verdict
slides.headline: Watch it play out.

slides.kicker: Lesson 3 · A loss isn’t a verdict
slides.headline: Process or outcome?
slides.do: Drop each statement in the right place.
slides.dayli: The stop getting hit doesn’t rewrite the trade that existed before it.

slides.kicker: Lesson 3 · A loss isn’t a verdict
slides.headline: After this loss, should the strategy change?

options.label: Yes, it lost
options.say: Based on what? Every check passed. One outcome isn’t a sample.

options.label: No, not from one valid loss
options.say: Right. Nothing in the process failed.

options.label: I need more data first
options.say: Fair. And one trade isn’t data.

slides.dayli: One valid loss is a cost of the method, not evidence against it.

takeaways: A valid loss is graded on process, like a valid win.
Don’t change a method because of one outcome.
remember: The stop getting hit does not rewrite the trade that existed before the stop got hit.
